discovery: The optical lattice clock and precision measurement at the 10^-18 level

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock, trapping many neutral atoms in a 'magic-wavelength' lattice so the clock transition is unperturbed by the trap. This removed the trade-off between Doppler-free confinement and large atom number. Katori and Ye turned the idea into instruments with fractional uncertainty and stability near 10^-18, about a hundredfold better than caesium standards. Ye's group added ultrastable lasers, degenerate Fermi-gas clocks and control of quantum many-body effects in the clock itself. These clocks have resolved gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences on a single sample and set new limits on variation of fundamental constants and on dark matter. They also point toward a redefinition of the second and toward relativistic geodesy. The field was built by lowering noise, extending coherence and inventing new ways to measure. Many laboratories worldwide now use it.
